description: Use this when a pose lacks the camera angle the user wants (get_pose lists the views a pose has). It makes a view of one of the pose's mannequins from another place on the Camera Angles globe: the mannequin's front picture is turned there, a check confirms it is the same pose and where the camera landed, and the view joins the shared pose library for EVERYONE, with its own mention (there are no private views). figure: woman or man, the one matching the character's gender (a mention sends that one; woman when unknown). azimuth, where the camera stands, in steps of 45: 0 front, 45 front right, 90 right side (the camera moved to the viewer's right, so the figure's LEFT side shows), 135 back right, 180 back, 225 back left, 270 left side, 315 front left (the pose's own three-quarter picture). elevation: 0 eye level, 30 from above, 60 from high above. A place that already has a view answers at once, free. Otherwise a job starts: it usually takes 30-90 seconds, so poll check_pose_view with the returned job_id every 10-15 seconds. 40 credits, charged only when the view lands where asked (a second try is free); a try that lands on another empty place is kept there for everyone, free. If someone is already making that view, you join their job for free. Up to 50 new views a day. Once done, write the view's mention after a character: "@barry in @seiza_pose.back" (.front_right, .right, .back_right, .back, .back_left, .left, .three_quarter, .above = front from above, .top = front from high above; other places a code like .az135_el30).

azimuth.description: Where the camera stands around the figure: 0 front, 45 front right, 90 right side (the camera moved to the viewer's right, so the figure's LEFT side shows), 135 back right, 180 back, 225 back left, 270 left side, 315 front left.

elevation.description: How high the camera stands: 0 eye level, 30 from above, 60 from high above.

figure.description: The mannequin to turn: the one that matches the character's gender (a mention sends that one); woman when it isn't known.

handle.description: The pose's handle, with or without the @ (e.g. "seiza_pose"), from search_poses or get_pose.
